steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Over here! I see him.

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: Coming, coming.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Hello.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: It's done. Have a look.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Wow...

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: Did you really make this?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I didn't expect it to be so fast. It's so cute!

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: I had inspiration when making it, so it took less time than I thought. Any part you'd like to change?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: None whatsoever. It's exactly how I imagined it!

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Here's the payment. And have some cookies too—we made them a couple of days ago in the kitchen.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Cookies? Thanks.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: The more I look at it, the more I like it. The collar padding's so nice! Soft and cushy.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: I tried a few materials, but this was the softest.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Picking the right one took quite a bit of time.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Did you make it in the dorms? The materials took up a lot of space, didn't they? I remember getting my head chewed off for taking up too much of the shared space when I was obsessed with toy blocks.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Are your roommates okay with this? I wouldn't want to cause you any trouble.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: No problem, they know about my hobby.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Operator Bibeak submitted an application for a sewing room. Maybe you can talk to the Logistics Department too, so that you don't have to keep everything piled up in your dorm.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Or even open a stall on the ship!

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Bibeak only makes clothes for the people she chooses, while Orchid specializes in coordinating outfits. You'd corner the market if you opened up a stall!

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: From the look on your face, you haven't talked to them yet?

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Yeah... Chiave may have recommended me to you, but I've never really thought about making clothes and accessories for anyone else.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: I've never even heard of the two operators you just mentioned.

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: Well, Bibeak and Orchid are easy to get along with. I'm sure there wouldn't be a problem if you wanted to chat with them.

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: Oh look, that was Bibeak just now!

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Did someone say my name?

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Oh, er, excuse me.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: This is my storeroom.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I also invited Orchid today, to teach the other operators design. Feel free to share your sewing knowledge too, if you like.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: I only came because I had a few questions for you. Not sure how much I can teach.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: It's fine. I don't really know enough to teach others either; I just wanted other people to talk about sewing with. Thanks for coming anyway!

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Bibeak? I'm here.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Orchid!

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Who's this?

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Hello ma'am, my name is Aosta. I'll be joining the lessons today.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: No need to be so polite. Hard to believe there are still well-mannered kids like you on Rhodes Island... Oh.

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: What a relief. I thought I'd be the only male operator here.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Sorry, did I keep everyone waiting? I brought some snacks for break time.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Thank you. Now let's get started!
Hushed but excited discussion fills the storeroom, as everyone inside is drawn into the world of sewing.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: (I'm not sure I should ask now.)

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: (Seems like they all know each other. Should I try to join the conversation?)

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: (Bibeak and Orchid... Originium crystals... Oh.)

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: (They have Oripathy too...)

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: (But they look so happy. Is it because they found a hobby they love?)

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: (...This storeroom's filled with Bibeak's materials. No wonder that operator suggested that I apply.)

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: Excuse me, do you know how to knit this kind of yarn pouch? It's supposed to be a gift, but I just can't get the hang of it.

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: The others are all busy right now, so I thought I'd ask you.
Bibeak and Orchid look completely immersed in their conversations.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Alright, let me have a look.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: You mean the one in this picture, right?

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: I see... it's a rather complicated pattern. Doing this on the right worktable would make things so much easier...

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: Something like this?

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Yes. Let me try it out and see if I'm on the right track. Give me a minute.

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: Sure, thanks.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: ...Maybe this kind of yarn would give it a better sheen.

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: Yeah, the colors look warmer under the light. I think she'll like it.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: ...Stringing a few beads here will make it look—I'm not sure how to put this, but more elaborate?

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: Let me see...

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: Wow. Your name's Aosta, right? Do you take orders?

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Huh? Yeah, I suppose. What do you ne—

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: Hey, did you rip your sleeve?

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: There's a nail sticking out here. I guess it got caught on it.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: It's fine. Nothing a little needlework can't fix.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Excuse me. Where are the needles?

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Behind you, in the drawers... third from the top? Or was it the fourth?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Do you need any thread too? And I have more materials in the box. Help yourself.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Thanks, just the needle and thread should be fine.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Oh, you're mending your own clothes?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: It can't be easy to sew while you're still wearing it.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: How about you take off your jacket? We have plenty of materials here. You can use this table.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Come on, let me fix that hole up.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Where's the thread? There's a spool here... is this white or black? Did you have a mud-throwing party in here or what?

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Hm... patterned? Not sure. Who cares, as long as it works!

steps.name: Broca
steps.text: Don't forget we still need some new fabric to make more clothes after this.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: And we can't cheap out on it either. I learned my lesson last year.

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: That dye was awful. Gave me rashes for days.

steps.name: Broca
steps.text: That's why you need to wash it a few times before wearing it.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Oh, I've always done it like this.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: This cloth is really durable. Just stitch it up a little, and it's good for a while.

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: But you used the good stuff when you knitted that yarn pouch for me.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: That's because I was doing it for you.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: When it's a job, I want to do it right. But my own clothes are made from durable materials, with thick threads that are made to last—

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: What's the matter?

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: Oh, it looks like you also got a scratch on your elbow from that nail. You didn't feel it?

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Just a little scrape. It's not bleeding anymore, I'll just wipe it down.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: A scratch? Let me see... yes. I always bring a few band-aids with me, because you never know when they'll come in handy.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Let me see your elbow. I have a first-aid kit with me too... Wait, why am I so used to this?

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Never mind. Over here.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: You don't need to—

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: We need to disinfect it.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: ...Yes, ma'am.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Hehe.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Even a small scratch can be big problem if there's any rust on the nail and the wound's not properly disinfected.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: ...Oh? That expression looks familiar. Let me guess... you hardly think it's a wound at all, don't you?

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Regardless of how you used to do things, you're on Rhodes Island now.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Make the most of your environment.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Hm... Looks good. Thanks.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: I'll get back to work then.

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: I can handle the rest myself. I was watching you work, and it was supposed to be a gift from me anyway. It's not right for me to ask that of someone who just ripped their clothes AND their elbow.

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: I'm really grateful though. Tell you what, I'll buy you a new jacket the next time we're on a mission together!

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: Ever since I was little, I've always wanted to earn money so I could buy gifts for everyone who helped me out. And now you're one of them, my man!

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: There's something that I've been thinking about all day.

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Lay it on me.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: When you were little, did you ever think about what you wanted to be when you grew up?

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Oh? Let me think... the head of the Famiglia, I guess?

steps.name: Broca
steps.text: Can't say I have...

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Well, for me...

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Before I ever picked up a weapon, before my dad brought me along with him...

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: I wanted to be a public official, to live a quiet and peaceful life.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Your needlework could be bolder, don't worry about ruining the cloth. It's the same for everyone at first, and even if you leave a hole there are ways to fix that.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Put your ideas into action. Don't be afraid to fail.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: You want to hide the Originium on your body? No problem, I can arrange things so no one sees it.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: But lately I've been thinking, why should we have to hide it?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I've thought about that too...

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Let me finish this up.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: (Oh, I wanted to chat with them.)

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: (...But now I don't feel like I need to?)

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: (I've never been able to figure this stuff out.)

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: Aosta?

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Oh, excuse me. I drifted off for a moment.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Once I'm done with this pouch, can you come help me pick out fabric to patch my jacket with?

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: I want to hear what you think.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: So you've come around at last.

steps.name: Serious Operator
steps.text: I'm coming too!

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Thank you.
Perhaps this is the way of life he wanted. Perhaps he could seize it with his own hands.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: They made me take all this fabric...

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: I should make something to thank them.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: And what Bibeak said... she wants me to experiment more. She says she's glad she came out of her own shell...

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: He—llo!!

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Whoa?!

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Hey, guess what I just did!

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Not interested.

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: I blew them all away!

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Hey, don't go!

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Look at this! Look who won first place!

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: That's right, ME!

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Winner of the 1st Rhodes Island cookie-eating contest, at 26 cookies! The undisputed champ!

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: There were people willing to play along with you? And you didn't get a royal beating from the cafeteria staff? Lucky bastard.

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Hey, if I ate it, it's not going to waste.

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: So where's Broca?

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: I have to tell him what a killjoy you are!

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Killjoy? Go brag to him, then. I'll be waiting for news of your victory to make the headlines of Rhodes Island Daily.

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Then I'll—wait, we have a newspaper here?

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Nope.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: You could feature in the first issue.

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: I know you're making fun of me! I'm not THAT stupid!

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Whatever. Is that Broca I just saw? See ya!

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Hahaha, I'm the champion!

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Hahaha, look at me! Look at this drawing I made!

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: What exactly is this?

steps.name: Broca
steps.text: ...Whoa.

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Don't you see? It shows how I beat up the thugs of the Famiglia!

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: Oh, come on, you can laugh, you know. It's not like this is the first time we've had people on our tail. We can always shake 'em!

steps.name: Chiave
steps.text: The car's right here. Stop overthinking it!

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: ...Yeah.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: This place is... eerily safe.
Aosta holds the rolls of cloth samples in his hands. They're heavy, but warm and soft.
He looks towards Chiave, running off with his hair whipping around in the wind. In those strands of hair, Aosta sees true joy, not forced smiles.
Aosta steps forward.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: I'll be your assistant today, Doctor.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: What do you need of me?

options: Nothing for now, just take a seat.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Aosta
steps.text: Doctor, can I have a DIY room on the ship?
